The setting was interesting at first, but I just couldn't deal with the writing so I'm leaving this one unfinished.

В игре когда-то был русский язык, но его почему-то убрали и так и не вернули. Поэтому, если вы хотите сыграть в неё на русском языке, переходите в обсуждение и качайте русификатор.

Визуал в игре хороший, и такой стиль рисовки мне понравился. Девушки выглядят красиво и сексуально. Но в игре есть цензура, что очень портит впечатление. В игре есть два режима цензуры: “нормальный” и “гуляй рука, балдей писюн”. В нормальном режиме цензуры девушки будут постоянно одеты, и раздеваться будут только в секс-сценах. В секс-сценах вы сможете нормально оценить бубяхи девушек, но на остальных частях будет пиксельная цензура. В режиме “гуляй рука, балдей писюн” девушки будут постоянно раздеты, и даже при обычных разговорах можно оценить бубсы девушки по достоинству. Но этот режим не отключает пиксельную цензуру, и в секс-сценах пиксели останутся. Если вы хотите поиграть без этой пиксельной мозаики, советую скачать патч 18+.

This game saved my life.

I am 27.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.

After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.

I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.

Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you

While I'd like to support and encourage Flaming Firefly as a developer, I'm not able to fully endorse this game or justify the price point it is being offered. Treasure of a Blizzard is an interesting tale with some rather good artwork set in an imaginative world. I enjoyed both the plot concept and manner in which the story wanted to immerse me into the setting with music, art, and style. The problem is that we simply don't experience enough of the the story to become fully invested. The plot is propelled forward so quickly that it feels more like the highlighted summary of a great story where readers dip in and out of key scenes rather than being enveloped by it.

I felt deprived of the sense of wonder we might have come to know had the developer spent more time on building up the world, the plot, the characters, and allowed relationships to grow naturally rather than have them inexplicably sandwiched together. At one point, I simply laughed at how nonsensically the protagonist receives sexual favor from a wolf girl after meeting her for the first time and answering one vague question with an equally vague answer option. Sadly, much of the game experience continues much the same; at times with ambiguous choices leading to instant death.

I was able to clear about half of the game's content in two hours, though time played is about double due to what I am assuming is the somewhat poor translation. I can't imagine how any publisher would allow this to be released if it is originally English. Unfortunately, I found myself unmotivated to complete the story's remaining scenarios. I salute the developer for a fresh and interesting concept and add, with positive criticism, that it just falls too short to be called a complete work and fails even to compete with titles that are available to read at no cost on Steam.

This review may be a little long, but it is intended to provide insight for those of you who are on the fence regarding its purchase.

Three months ago I downloaded the game demo and it was OK, but didn’t seem to promise enough to be worth its list price, especially since some “choices matter” multiple ending games that I’ve played in the past (--cough--Crystalline--cough--) have “time bomb” consequences that may hit you hours of gameplay later after making a “wrong” choice. As a result, I uninstalled the demo and basically forgot about it. Recently Treasure of a Blizzard went on sale and after further procrastination I decided to go ahead and purchase it. I am glad I did.

Review

Based on my history with other “choices matter” games, the first thing I did was look for a guide. There are several. The guide “FULL FLOW DIAGRAM” by derailed_omega_male was sufficient for me to feel I had my “safety net,” (It shows in a very large graphic the flow of the game without detailing what happens.)

That done, I found the game extremely entertaining and admit that when patched with 18+ content it is worth the asking price. The results of the game choices are (in my opinion) occasionally unpredictable, so I suspect that without using a guide, you are likely to end up where you don’t really want to end up. In any case, you can always go through the game once and then use a guide to “clean up” your results. This gives you options.

The written dialogue is clever, but there are spelling and grammar errors. The artwork is good or better throughout and is all in the same style, so there are no jarring visual transitions that I noticed. They could have used another sprite or two for each of the four main characters, since occasionally a particular character’s expression didn’t quite fit the dialogue at the time.

Based on my experience, and what I saw in the guide I referenced, much of the game has some tolerance for making “imperfect choices,” but there are a few cases where a seemingly minor choice will tank your result. Therefore, be aware that you might be disappointed with the ending of your first playthrough if you do not use a guide.

Adult content

This is not an H game, although it includes adult situations and graphics. Each adult scene is only one or two images, so 98% of this game is a choices matter story. If you are looking for an H game, you will probably not enjoy Treasure of a Blizzard. If you want a choices matter game with some explicit, story related content, this game will be right down your alley.

If you don’t use the patch, the game uses both mosaic censoring and some white glowing stars (such as would be “sprinkled” around a picture of a magical item) that are placed over “special” areas. I prefer the “star” censoring to the use of mosaics.

There is a patch available that removes almost all** censorship, but it is not available not on Steam. According to the publisher, they cannot supply the patch either, since it violates some of their local laws. Still, a patch is available and since that patch source was referenced by the publisher (wink), it does seem to be OK to use. I can confirm that it does remove almost all** censoring and does not seem to affect the game or its stability in any way.

** Note: Even with the patch, there is at least one CG I saw that still had the star censoring (in what would otherwise have been a pretty amazing image). I have only completed 3 of the 10 endings, so there may be more.

Recommended.

Hello Steam user who is wondering if this little visual novel is worth their time. I'm going to tell you right now that the answer is yes especially especially considering that it has a nice winter wonderland theme to match with the holidays.

Pros
– Art, the character designs specifically. I feel like everyone's designs were uniquely suited for their characters, like for instance Mei's mischievous smile or Kang's smug grin felt distinctly their own that if you put those expressions on another character it would just look wrong. Also speaking of distinctive, I feel like I haven't seen these character designs before or at least not these [i]exact[/i] character designs before. Yes that seems a bit like an overstatement by hear me out. The designs are polished enough so it doesn't look like deviant art amateur hour garbage but not so polished that they give off the generic professional glam look that I tend to see with a lot more big-budget visual novels. It feels unique to this game and that's something I appreciate even if the art isn't dropdead gorgeous.
– The characters. I would nearly appreciate the character designs as well as I do if I didn't like the characters themselves but thankfully the characters do match up to their designs. Of our four main characters, Kang and the lovely werewolf Shan were definitely my favorites but I also appreciated Lin's[spoiler]money fetish[/spoiler]stick and[spoiler]Mei's thinly veiled selfish attitude[/spoiler]. These characters felt like characters which is more than I can say for some visual novels where literally [i]nobody[/i] has a personality or has the most bare-bones basic personality that you could get off a cardboard box. Everybody had both their strengths and their weaknesses for instance, Kang is a cynical asshat with a serious drinking problem but that doesn't mean he doesn't care about his childhood friend Lin or his father and (depending on your choices, the other two girls problems as well) I wouldn't necessarily call him the greatest person out there but I wouldn't say he's a bad person which is pretty much the sentiment I have for the other characters as well they have their issues but they're not inherently bad people. They'll kinda live in a gray area and most people in real life live there so I definitely appreciated that aspect of the game.
– The endings. I like how this game definitely had a variety of endings as opposed to all of them feeling sane the same like I've seen some visual novels have. The game has ten endings in every ending feels distinctly different. Naturally some of them are the happily ever after endings and of course there are a few endings where you die but interestingly, one of the [i]worst[/i] ending in the entire game isn't even an ending where you die... I'm not gonna spoil it but let's just say it's a emotional got wrenching ending the say the least.

Cons
– price. Okay this is probably get to be the biggest complaint but for how long this game actually takes (I think I completed all the endings in four hours though I will admit I was using the skip button after my first initial run) the prices a little steep.
– the music. Okay I actually liked the music. The reason of putting it on the cons list though is because I feel like it was missed used in a few places. Like during this one scene where[spoiler]Mei is really mad at you for explaining her plan for the crystals to Shan what's playing is this bombastic music that's completely distracting when it should of been something more somber or emotion filled music since this is a pinnacle choice in the game aim especially if your aiming for one of her endings.[/spoiler]There are other places where this happens but this one was the most glaring.

Neutral
– the story. It's not a bad story but I wouldn't call it revolutionary either. Fairly standard little fantasy romp with monster fights, hints of prejudice and magic but not that all things considered.


Anyway, with all things considered I think I will recommend the game, for the art and characters if nothing else. Though I will say it's probably best to get it on a sale.

The game is not as kitschy as it might look like. It directly/indirectly mentions pretty serious subjects including, but not limited to: dictatorship, xenophobia, uprisings in times of hardship and iron-fisted supression of the uprisings, alcoholism, gambling, betrayal, lies, fear of the unknown, law of the strongest, being forced to do things against your will (including risking of your life and outright slavery) and of course romance.

I didn't expect it, but I actually ended up enjoying the story. (You get to see most of the story from the 3rd person perspective, but you still hear the story including the protagonist's thoughts from the 1st person perspective.) The art and the music also deserve praise. The game has [spoiler]10[/spoiler] possible endings and a nice collection of CGs. The [spoiler]four[/spoiler] main characters are interesting and each one of them is crazy in his own unique way (One is [spoiler]an alcoholic[/spoiler], one is obsessed with [spoiler]money[/spoiler], one [spoiler]seems to be nice but might end up enslaving you due to jealousy[/spoiler], one acts[spoiler]by the law of the strongest and orders you around while threatening to kill you if you don't obey[/spoiler]). I played the game until I unlocked everything and understood the whole structure of decisions, which took approximately 40 hours.

H-scenes can be also included by applying an official H-patch, but prepare to be [spoiler]slightly disappointed due to a very low amount of text in the H-scenes[/spoiler].

Background of the story (insignificant spoilers, I'm not even going to black the section out):

The story takes place in a fabulous world with magic and magical creatures. Although magic seems to be rare and some people still don't believe in it's existence. There are at least two major political regions:
One of the regions is a xenophobic dictatorial empire brutally ruled by an iron fist (insurgency of poor population in times of hardship is considered a high treason and leads to executions). Magical creatures don't have equal rights compared to ordinary people. The xenophobia towards magical creatures and witchcraft is especially strong amongst peasants. Other classes of population seems to be a little bit more tolerant towards magic and even have a small amount of magical "blood in their veins".
The other region is a significantly more liberal and more tolerant union of kingdoms. The world outside doesn't know mutch about the union. Many people and magical creatures seems to escape from the empire and migrate to the union, but they rarely return.
The actual story doesn't take place in the kingdoms and not in the empire (or at least not the the cities of the empire), but in the wilderness.

How the story begins (bigger spoilers, but not very big spoilers):

[spoiler]Two former childhood friends are travelling to the empire's capital city. One of them is forced to move to the capital against his will to live under surveillance for a crime of feeding some starving insurgent peasants comitted by his father. The other one is loyal to the empire and is supposed to keep his former friend under captivity. Surprised by an extraordinary cold weather they are forced to seek shelter in a solitary house in order to survive. Soon they are forced to help strangers by risking their lives against their own will. (Or at least the first traveller is.) [/spoiler]

Что в этой игре есть хорошего:
* [b]Графика.[/b] Отрисованные фоны, приятные анимешные девочки. Над визуальной частью действительно постарались, к этому нет никаких претензий -- это было красиво.
*[b]NC.[/b] В конце концов это эроге, а значит без потрахулечек с тяночками не обойдется.
Ммм.. И все? По крайней мере мне это было единственное, что понравилось мне.

Что в игре есть плохого:
* [b]Музыка.[/b] Нет, она довольно приятная. но неуместная -- слишком активная  в спокойных моментах; слишком громкая, даже после того как найдешь заветный рычажок. при этом эффектов самой игры за этой музыкой я не услышала
* [b]Сюжет.[/b] Он как бы есть, но его как бы нет. Если все ради чего игра задумывалась, это эротические сцены -- пожалуйста, но не надо наверчивать искренне недалекий и весьма скучный сюжет. Если же выходите добавить к поебулечкам сюжет, то делайте это пожалуйста... качественно.
* [b]Персонажки.[/b] Настолько блеклых существ я не видела давно. После знакомства с ними единственная концовка, которая стала для меня приемлемой -- без каждой из этих картонных кукол для ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Они красивые. да. Но их характеры -- это просто нет. Одна -- классическая цундере, которая с самого начала постоянно нас унижает, но в итоге при всех своих боевых навыках оказывается максимально бесполезной в сюжете. Вторая -- крайне сексуальная интригантка, которая помимо этой соблазнительной хитрости не имеет... ничего более в характере? Хотя изначально именно эта персонажка меня хоть чем-то порадовала, она оказалась столь же плоской (во всем кроме груди). Третья -- намек на характер (ура), но первое ее появление все что оставило -- это самодовольство и надменность. А теперь момент: ни с одной из эти девушек с первого их появления у меня не возникло желания завязать общения, а разве не в этом смысл эроге новелл?
*[b] NC.[/b] Да-да, не удивляйтесь. И здесь у меня вопрос скорее опять относящийся к сюжету. а конкретнее -- к завязке эротических сцен. Они начинаются настолько рандомно, что Станиславский во мне не только вопил "не верю", но и плакал кровавыми слезами. Чего только стоит первая эротическая сцена с волко-девочкой [spoiler] с минетом в лесу[/spoiler]. Это заставляет скорее сфэйспамить чем вздрочнуть.
